title: Efficiency Gains from Guaranteed First-Stage Reward Recording in Two-Stage Policy Evaluation
banked_reason: Supervisor-authorized proposal-stage abandonment after repeated applicability REVISE; documented give-up produced NO-PASS. Not a mathematical soundness verdict; closed, do not requeue.
gap_reasons: The jointly load-bearing exact normalized known-basis diagonal chart, fixed exponent-eight spectrum, and order-eighty history/source restrictions are expressly only synthetic and lack a credible realistic data-generating setting or calibration, so the claimed causal methods contribution needs an applicability bridge beyond witness laws.
proof_attempt_summary: Three proposal versions remained REVISE at field tier. Honest benchmark scope and a substantive exact gain/feasible certificate addition did not cure the repeated applicability finding. Supervisor authorized abandonment; the documented give-up action produced terminal NO-PASS. This failed-bucket entry is a proposal-stage archive, not a soundness verdict: no D0 derivation or Lean formalization was reached and all proposed claims remain unverified. Closed by operator; do not requeue or automatically re-raise. Reviews and validity decisions are retained; no Lean/API build, substrate promotion, presentation, or git commit was performed.
tldr: Guaranteed first reward recording changes the information available to a fixed second-stage policy. Exact uniform complete-case marginals, a known infinite Legendre-diagonal copula, exact density normalization, and fixed source and history-smoothness orders forty and eighty define an analytic measurement-decision benchmark rather than a credible generic applied regime. Within this benchmark, a feasible cross-fitted Wald interval for \(V_{\rm rec}\) estimates continuation, recording functions, diagonal coefficients and behavior propensities. An exact four-product drift supports its uniform expansion, and conditional mean-zero Legendre controls give the diagonal-model score. The field contribution includes a model-wide exact conditional Gram/Legendre formula for the variance gain, an if-and-only-if nonzero-control-moment criterion for strict gain, and a nonnegative held-out gain estimator with a uniformly valid thresholded certificate. A legal two-stage law has variances \(256/3\) and \(128/3\), with gain \(128/3\) supplied by two explicit control modes at each stage. A same-law polynomial/sign-reactive contrast excludes the sign policy from the interval class. Feasible uniform efficient Wald coverage is only under the declared benchmark class \(\mathcal C(\pi)\). Canonical-gradient attainment is only at strict interior laws of \(\mathcal M_D\) and does not transfer to the ambient \(\mathcal M_S\). Chen--Xie supplies the generic projection principle; the contribution is its conditional diagonal-shadow specialization and feasible certification in an incremental technical methods note. The policy-dependent feasibility frontier remains open. No clinical validation is claimed.
gap: One-time shadow representers, sequential augmentation, natural-recording evaluation, MNAR policy intervals and generic efficiency projection already exist. The narrow gap is a checkable conditional diagonal-shadow gain formula, its exact strict-gain criterion, and a feasible observable certificate together with primitive uniform interval attainment for guaranteed first recording.
fill: Conditional mean-zero controls, their explicit stagewise Gram/Legendre blocks, the exact gain criterion, and independent squared fitted projections quantify and certify \(\Delta(P)\). Primitive nuisance concentration, the normalized finite catalogue, four-product drift and uniform projection approximation supply the efficient interval. Feasible uniform efficient Wald coverage is only under the declared benchmark class \(\mathcal C(\pi)\). Canonical-gradient attainment is only at strict interior laws of \(\mathcal M_D\) and does not transfer to the ambient \(\mathcal M_S\).
